_meta.indication: DOTAREM is a gadolinium-based contrast agent indicated for intravenous use with MRI in brain (intracranial), spine and associated tissues in adult and pediatric patients (2 years of age and older) to detect and visualize areas with disruption of the blood brain barrier (BBB) and/or abnormal vasculature.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, international, randomized, double-blind, fixed-sequence (unenhanced MRI followed by Dotarem- or Magnevist-enhanced MRI), active-comparator study with patients serving as their own control; Dotarem 0.1 mmol/kg.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and pediatric patients referred for contrast-enhanced MRI of the CNS with a suspected CNS abnormality; 364 adults randomized 2:1 Dotarem:Magnevist (245 Dotarem, 119 Magnevist) plus 38 pediatric patients aged 2-18 years assigned to the Dotarem group (37 pediatric subjects were included in the Full Analysis Set).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Within-group superiority of “Paired” (unenhanced + Dotarem-enhanced) over unenhanced (“Pre”) images for three co-primary lesion-visualization variables: border delineation, internal morphology, and degree of contrast enhancement.
pivotal_trials.n: 357 adults administered contrast (Dotarem 240, Magnevist 117); 393 subjects in the Full Analysis Set (356 adults, 37 pediatric).
pivotal_trials.result: Study met all components of its primary endpoint: Paired images were superior to Pre (unenhanced) images for all 3 co-primary variables for all 3 readers, with p < 0.001 for all within-group comparisons.

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3 (re-read of a single-arm Dotarem study)
pivotal_trials.design: Non-randomized, single-arm Dotarem study consisting of a blinded re-reading of original MRI images from the earlier phase 3 trial DGD-3-44, designed with an analysis identical to study -050; referral limited to tumoral disease only.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients referred for MRI of cerebral or spinal tumors; 149 subjects in the Full Analysis Set.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Within-group superiority of “Paired” (Dotarem-enhanced) over unenhanced (“Pre”) images for the same three co-primary lesion-visualization variables (border delineation, internal morphology, contrast enhancement).
pivotal_trials.result: Paired images were superior to unenhanced images for all 3 co-primary variables for all 3 readers with a statistically significant difference of p < 0.001 for each.

key_safety: Overall 3.9% of patients reported at least one adverse reaction; the most frequent (≥0.2%) were nausea (0.6%), headache (0.5%), injection site pain (0.4%), injection site coldness (0.2%) and burning sensation (0.2%). The most serious risks are nephrogenic systemic fibrosis and hypersensitivity/anaphylactoid reactions.
target_moa: Dotarem is a macrocyclic paramagnetic gadolinium chelate; the gadolinium ion has paramagnetic properties due to its 7 unpaired electrons, and when placed in a magnetic field it shortens T1 and T2 relaxation times of water protons, producing contrast enhancement in MRI.
modality: other (gadolinium-based MRI contrast agent / small-molecule gadolinium chelate)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: NEPHROGENIC SYSTEMIC FIBROSIS (NSF) — GBCAs increase the risk for NSF among patients with impaired elimination of the drugs; avoid use in these patients unless the diagnostic information is essential and not available with non-contrasted MRI or other modalities. NSF may result in fatal or debilitating fibrosis affecting the skin, muscle and internal organs.

advisory_committee.vote: Medical Imaging Advisory Committee (MIDAC) met February 14, 2013. The committee voted unanimously that Dotarem demonstrated efficacy and a favorable risk/benefit for adults and pediatric patients aged 2 years and older; in a 6-10-1 vote (yes-no-abstention) it voted against approval for pediatric patients younger than 2 years of age.

description.text: Expanded Dotarem MRI use to brain, spine and associated tissues in adult and pediatric patients including term neonates to detect blood brain barrier disruption and/or abnormal vascularity

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for intravenous use of Dotarem with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in brain (intracranial), spine and associated tissues in adult and pediatric patients (including term neonates) to detect and visualize areas with disruption of the blood brain barrier (BBB) and/or abnormal vascularity.

basis.text: The application was reviewed under Priority designation.

summary.text: Dotarem (gadoterate meglumine) is a new molecular entity gadolinium-based MRI contrast agent that received Priority review and standard (non-accelerated) approval on March 20, 2013 based on two phase 3 trials (DGD-44-050 and DGD-44-051); a Medical Imaging Advisory Committee convened on February 14, 2013, and pediatric PREA studies in the 0-23 month age group were deferred as required post-marketing studies.

citations.quote: Chemical class: This product is a new molecular entity (NME).
Dotarem was the subject of a meeting of the Medical Imaging Advisory Committee (MIDAC) held on February 14, 2013.
The applicant met the primary efficacy endpoints in both pivotal trials (DGD-44-050 and DGD-44-051)

We are deferring submission of your pediatric studies that assess Dotarem in the 0-23 month age group until June 30, 2016, because this product is ready for approval for use in adults and pediatric patient aged two years and older.

requirement.text: Study 2021-1: Provide additional nonclinical (animal) data to support the safety of the product in the 0-23 month pediatric age group, obtained from newborn to juvenile animals that model pediatric patients in this age group.

citations.quote: Study 2021-1: Provide additional nonclinical (animal) data to support the safety of your product in the 0-23 month pediatric age group. These nonclinical data should be obtained from newborn to juvenile animals that model pediatric patients in this age group.

requirement.text: Study 2021-2: Study patients 0-23 months of age referred for a contrast MRI exam; at least 40 patients to adequately characterize pharmacokinetics and support safety and efficacy in this age group.

citations.quote: Study 2021-2: Examine patients 0-23 months of age who are referred for an MRI exam with contrast. A sufficient number of subjects will be studied to adequately characterize the pharmacokinetics of the product in this age group. At least 40 patients will be evaluated in this study
